speaker: Nikos
content: Welcome everyone. This is the Q3 roadmap planning session. Goal today: agree the top three initiatives and rough owners.

speaker: Priya
content: Before we dive in, can we timebox? I have a hard stop in an hour.

speaker: Nikos
content: Yes, one hour. We'll spend twenty minutes on candidates, twenty on prioritisation, twenty on owners and risks.

speaker: Sarah
content: Sounds good. I'll capture decisions as we go.

speaker: Mike
content: I've got three candidate initiatives from engineering: the billing rewrite, the mobile app, and the data platform.

speaker: Tom
content: Sales is pushing hard for the mobile app. Three of our biggest accounts asked for it last quarter.

speaker: Nadia
content: Support would vote for the billing rewrite. Billing errors are our number one ticket driver right now.

speaker: Nikos
content: Let's get all candidates on the table first, then prioritise. Mike, expand on the billing rewrite.

speaker: Mike
content: The current billing system is a tangle of cron jobs. It's brittle, hard to change, and it's blocking three other features.

speaker: Nadia
content: From support's side, customers get double-charged maybe twice a month. Each incident is hours of manual cleanup.

speaker: Sarah
content: That double-charging issue — is there a quick fix, or does it genuinely need the rewrite?

speaker: Mike
content: There's a band-aid, but the root cause is the architecture. A real fix means the rewrite.

speaker: Priya
content: What's the rough size of the billing rewrite?

speaker: Mike
content: Two engineers for most of the quarter. Call it ten engineer-weeks.

speaker: Tom
content: The mobile app is bigger revenue upside though. Those three accounts are worth a lot of annual recurring revenue.

speaker: Nikos
content: Tom, can you put a number on the mobile app opportunity?

speaker: Tom
content: Conservatively, retaining those three accounts is a big chunk of next year's renewal. Plus it opens a new segment.

speaker: Priya
content: And the cost? Mobile is a different skill set than we have in-house.

speaker: Mike
content: Right, we'd need to either hire or contract. That's a hiring lead time of two to three months.

speaker: Nadia
content: If we do mobile first, billing stays broken all quarter and support keeps bleeding.

speaker: Sarah
content: Let me note the tension: mobile is revenue upside but slow to start; billing is cost-saving and ready to go.

speaker: Nikos
content: Good framing. What about the data platform, Mike?

speaker: Mike
content: The data platform is foundational. It unblocks analytics, ML, and better reporting for everyone.

speaker: Priya
content: Foundational is the problem though. It's the kind of project that's hard to justify on its own this quarter.

speaker: Tom
content: Sales can't sell a data platform. We can sell a mobile app.

speaker: Nadia
content: Support can't deflect tickets with a data platform either, at least not this quarter.

speaker: Nikos
content: So the data platform is important but maybe not urgent. Let's park it as a candidate and revisit.

speaker: Sarah
content: Parked: data platform, important-not-urgent, revisit in Q4 planning.

speaker: Priya
content: Okay so realistically it's billing versus mobile for the top slot.

speaker: Nikos
content: Let's do a quick prioritisation pass. I'll use impact, effort, and time-to-value.

speaker: Mike
content: Billing: high impact on cost and reliability, medium effort, fast time-to-value.

speaker: Tom
content: Mobile: high impact on revenue, high effort, slow time-to-value because of hiring.

speaker: Priya
content: On those numbers, billing wins on time-to-value clearly.

speaker: Tom
content: But mobile wins on strategic upside. We can't keep deferring it or we lose the accounts.

speaker: Nadia
content: Could we sequence them? Billing this quarter, start mobile hiring in parallel?

speaker: Nikos
content: That's interesting. The hiring lead time for mobile is dead time anyway.

speaker: Mike
content: Yes — if we start recruiting mobile engineers now, they onboard just as billing wraps.

speaker: Sarah
content: So proposed sequence: billing rewrite as the Q3 deliverable, mobile hiring kicks off in parallel immediately.

speaker: Priya
content: I like that. It uses the hiring lead time instead of wasting it.

speaker: Tom
content: I can live with that if we commit to a real mobile start date. I don't want it to slip forever.

speaker: Nikos
content: Fair. Let's set a checkpoint: mobile development starts at the beginning of Q4, non-negotiable.

speaker: Tom
content: Good. I'll set expectations with the three accounts that mobile lands early next year.

speaker: Nadia
content: And billing improvements ship this quarter, which I can communicate to the noisiest customers.

speaker: Mike
content: One risk: the two engineers for billing are also the only two who know the payments integration.

speaker: Priya
content: That's a bus-factor risk. If either gets pulled onto an incident, billing slips.

speaker: Nikos
content: Mitigation? Can we cross-train a third engineer partway through?

speaker: Mike
content: We can pair a third engineer in from week three to spread the knowledge. Slight cost to velocity.

speaker: Sarah
content: Risk noted: billing bus-factor, mitigation is to pair in a third engineer from week three.

speaker: Priya
content: What about the mobile hiring risk? Two to three months is optimistic in this market.

speaker: Tom
content: If hiring slips, the Q4 start slips. That's the real schedule risk.

speaker: Nikos
content: Can we de-risk hiring by lining up a contractor as a fallback?

speaker: Mike
content: Yes, a contractor bridge would let us start Q4 even if full-time hiring runs late.

speaker: Sarah
content: Risk noted: mobile hiring may slip, mitigation is a contractor bridge to protect the Q4 start.

speaker: Nadia
content: Should we also budget some support engineering time for the billing migration cutover?

speaker: Mike
content: Good call. Cutover weekends will generate tickets. We should have support on standby.

speaker: Nadia
content: I'll schedule a support rota for the cutover weekend once we know the date.

speaker: Nikos
content: Let's pin a tentative cutover for the last week of the quarter, with a fallback the week after.

speaker: Sarah
content: Tentative billing cutover: last week of Q3, fallback first week of Q4.

speaker: Priya
content: On owners — who owns billing end to end?

speaker: Mike
content: I'll own the billing rewrite. Two engineers under me, third paired in from week three.

speaker: Nikos
content: Mike owns billing. Who owns the mobile hiring track?

speaker: Priya
content: I can own mobile hiring with recruiting. I'll drive the pipeline and the contractor fallback.

speaker: Nikos
content: Priya owns mobile hiring. Tom, you own the account communication for both.

speaker: Tom
content: Agreed. I'll own messaging to the three accounts and the broader sales narrative.

speaker: Nadia
content: I'll own the support readiness for the billing cutover — rota, runbook, and customer comms.

speaker: Sarah
content: Owners captured: Mike billing, Priya mobile hiring, Tom account comms, Nadia support readiness.

speaker: Nikos
content: Excellent. Let's talk budget briefly. Does the contractor fallback fit this quarter's budget?

speaker: Priya
content: A contractor bridge is within the contingency budget if we only trigger it on a hiring slip.

speaker: Nikos
content: Good. So it's a conditional spend, not a committed one.

speaker: Priya
content: Correct. Committed spend is the two billing engineers and recruiting fees.

speaker: Sarah
content: Budget note: committed spend is billing engineers plus recruiting; contractor is conditional contingency.

speaker: Mike
content: One more dependency: the billing rewrite needs the new payments API key from finance.

speaker: Nikos
content: Who chases finance for the payments API key?

speaker: Mike
content: I'll chase finance, but it helps if it comes from you, Nikos, for priority.

speaker: Nikos
content: I'll send the request to finance today and copy you, Mike.

speaker: Sarah
content: Action: Nikos requests the payments API key from finance today, Mike copied.

speaker: Mike
content: Two plus the paired third from week three is the right size. Three from day one is overkill.

speaker: Tom
content: From a sales view, I just need the billing reliability message to be true by quarter end.

speaker: Nadia
content: And from support, fewer billing tickets by quarter end is the success metric.

speaker: Nikos
content: Let's define success metrics explicitly. Billing: reduce billing tickets by half by quarter end.

speaker: Nadia
content: Half is achievable if the double-charge root cause is fixed. I'll baseline current ticket volume.

speaker: Sarah
content: Success metric: halve billing tickets by end of Q3, baseline owned by Nadia.

speaker: Nikos
content: Mobile success metric for Q3 is just a staffed team ready to start Q4. Agreed?

speaker: Priya
content: Agreed. Q3 mobile success is a hired or contracted team ready for a Q4 kickoff.

speaker: Sarah
content: Success metric: mobile team staffed and ready for Q4 start by end of Q3.

speaker: Tom
content: Can we add a soft metric — no account churn from the three at-risk accounts this quarter?

speaker: Nikos
content: Yes, retention of the three accounts through Q3 is a shared metric for you and me, Tom.

speaker: Sarah
content: Success metric: retain all three at-risk accounts through Q3, shared Tom and Nikos.

speaker: Nikos
content: Let me synthesise. Q3: ship the billing rewrite, start mobile hiring in parallel, park the data platform.

speaker: Mike
content: Owners: me on billing, Priya on hiring, Tom on accounts, Nadia on support readiness.

speaker: Nadia
content: Metrics: halve billing tickets, staff the mobile team, retain the three accounts.

speaker: Tom
content: Risks: billing bus-factor and mobile hiring slip, both with mitigations.

speaker: Priya
content: And the Q4 mobile start is a hard commitment, not a soft hope.

speaker: Nikos
content: Any objections to that plan as stated? Last chance.

speaker: Sarah
content: None from me. I have it all captured.

speaker: Mike
content: No objections.

speaker: Tom
content: No objections, provided the Q4 start holds.

speaker: Nadia
content: No objections.

speaker: Priya
content: Agreed. Good session.

speaker: Nikos
content: Then we're decided. Sarah will circulate the notes and action items by end of day. Thanks everyone.
